description: Steiner-Parker filter with a separate input for each response, so three sources can be filtered differently and mixed at one output, and a choice of three simulation models

params.text: Sets the frequency at which the filter starts to act: fully counter-clockwise it is closed, fully clockwise it is open
Boosts the frequencies near the cutoff, and past a point the filter self-oscillates
Attenuates and inverts the CUTOFF input before it is added to the cutoff, and a 1V/octave signal through it makes the cutoff track pitch
Attenuates and inverts the RESONANCE input before it is added to the resonance
Sets how much signal enters the filter, and raising it saturates the filter and adds harmonics
Attenuates and inverts the DRIVE input before it is added to the drive
Picks the simulation model: YU is the smooth default, MS adds diode clipping in the feedback path for a smoother resonance, XX is the wildest of the three

inputs.text: The signal patched here is low pass filtered
The signal patched here is band pass filtered
The signal patched here is high pass filtered
A control voltage added to the cutoff, scaled by the CUTOFF attenuverter, and tracking 1V per octave when that attenuverter is set for it
A control voltage added to the resonance, scaled by the RESONANCE attenuverter
A control voltage added to the drive, scaled by the DRIVE attenuverter

outputs.text: The three filtered inputs mixed together
